purpose: Compare two scenario-only relative elevation grids on B42 peninsula/inner-sea eastern mainland. Explore possible R1/R2 drainage partition without claiming measured terrain.

frame.sea_or_other_polygon_labels: Outside polygon 0 is masked as zero-height in this local study; possible other land not comprehensively modeled.

method.A: Outlet-conditioned least-cost surface: seed R1/R2 candidate coast cells; Dijkstra in mainland with travel cost rising with distance from the corresponding B43 schematic route. Minimum two positive costs produces synthetic divides. This is deliberately inverse-constrained, NOT independent geological corroboration.
method.B: Independent simple inland-easterly tilt plus midlatitude broad ridge and small smooth disturbances. No candidate mouth or river route is used in constructing B heights.
method.routing: D8 steepest descent on synthetic relative relief; 8 connected neighbors; non-land neighbor as zero; no depression filling; edge escapes and sinks separately labeled.
method.labeling: R1 or R2 when traced sea-exit cell is within 45 illustration units of B43 mouth; not exclusive complete geological basin. OTHER_COAST for elsewhere; DOMAIN_EDGE and SINK remain unresolved.
method.rainfall: Equal single unit per land raster cell for sample flow accumulation; no real precipitation, runoff or discharge.
limits: The grid covers an eastern continental study window, not the entire planet.
Relief 0-255 is dimensionless; no surveyed elevations or geologic uplift rates.
B43 lines were themselves only feasible schematic corridors.
Comparing a route-conditioned construction with an unconditioned tilt is a sensitivity demonstration, not a test that decides what nature did.
D8 on a coarse grid has artifacts, diagonal bias and possible pits; flow accumulation in cells is not river flow.
Do not convert sample stream traces to officially accepted rivers or watershed boundaries.

next: Inspect map-scale catchment fractions, determine whether scenario A is too forced or creates topologically unreasonable divides.
Add local uplift and sediment provenance tests constrained by explicit geology evidence, without turning B39 remote-island highland probes into local observations.
